editorNotes.purpose: Instructions for an LLM or human editing this question bank. Keep this object when creating, editing, or deleting questions.
questionBankRules: Questions are stored in the questions array. Do not place question objects beside editorNotes.
Every question id must be unique, stable, lowercase kebab-case, and descriptive. Do not reuse an id from a deleted question for a different concept.
Every question must have exactly four plausible options and exactly one correct answer.
answerId must exactly match one option id. Option ids must be unique within their question and use lowercase kebab-case.
Explain every option independently. A learner should understand why each choice is right or wrong without comparing option positions.
Do not encode correctness through option order, wording length, certainty, grammar, or repeated phrases. The application shuffles options.
decisiveClue should name the minimum scenario evidence that makes the best answer defensible; do not merely repeat the answer.
Use realistic Aurora Outfitters work scenarios and assess transfer or judgment rather than isolated trivia whenever possible.
Avoid trick questions, double negatives, subjective wording, and distractors that are wrong only because of an unstated assumption.
Keep terminology aligned with current Microsoft Fabric and DP-600 documentation.
sourceId must match a key in content/sources.ts. Add or update that source registry when a question needs a new authoritative Microsoft Learn source.
objectiveIds must use the domain prefixes MAINTAIN, PREPARE, or MODEL and identify the smallest applicable DP-600 objectives.
remediation.href must be an internal hash route beginning with # and should lead to the closest relevant lesson or lab.
Set verifiedDate to the ISO date YYYY-MM-DD on which the answer was checked against the cited source.
status may be draft or reviewed during editing, but only verified questions should be shipped in the application.
Do not add misconceptionId to option objects. The application derives each incorrect option's misconception id from its option id and assigns null to the correct option.
When deleting a question, remove the complete question object and preserve valid JSON. Recheck coverage before deleting the only question for a difficulty, domain, or objective.

difficultyRubric.1: Foundation: one direct concept or clearly stated requirement; little or no competing evidence.
difficultyRubric.2: Core: apply one concept in a realistic scenario and distinguish it from plausible neighboring concepts.
difficultyRubric.3: Applied: combine multiple clues, preserve grain or context, or diagnose a consequence with credible distractors.
difficultyRubric.4: Advanced: reason through interacting Fabric behaviors, lifecycle constraints, security effects, fallback behavior, or non-obvious tradeoffs. Do not make a question advanced merely by using obscure terminology.

coverageGuidance: Maintain a reasonable spread across all four difficulty values; keep at least two verified questions at each difficulty.
Approximate the DP-600 blueprint over a larger bank: Maintain 25-30%, Prepare 45-50%, and Semantic models 25-30%.
Avoid repeatedly assessing the same objective just to satisfy domain totals. Prefer objectives with no or little coverage.
Difficulty is not learner ability. It describes the reasoning demand of this individual question.

questions.title: A governed retail reporting store
questions.context: Aurora needs to load structured sales transactions in batches. Finance analysts use T-SQL heavily and need governed enterprise BI reporting. Device telemetry is handled by another team.
questions.question: Where should Priya begin for this reporting workload?

options.label: Warehouse
options.explanation: Warehouse best matches structured relational data, T-SQL, and enterprise BI requirements.

options.label: Lakehouse
options.explanation: Lakehouse can support analytics and engineering, but the stated relational T-SQL reporting requirements make Warehouse the stronger fit.

options.label: Eventhouse
options.explanation: Eventhouse is intended for event and telemetry analysis, which the scenario explicitly puts elsewhere.

options.label: Power BI semantic model in Import mode
options.explanation: A semantic model is an analytical layer, not the governed relational store requested for loading and querying the transactions.

questions.decisiveClue: Structured transactions + T-SQL + governed BI are the requirements that matter; the telemetry detail is not part of this workload.

questions.title: One report, different regional views
questions.context: Jonas can open Aurora’s Sales report. He must see only Norway rows while Sweden managers use the same report and semantic model to see Sweden rows.
questions.question: Which control should Leila configure?

options.label: Row-level security on the semantic model
options.explanation: RLS filters model rows for the signed-in identity while allowing users to open the same report.

options.label: A separate item permission for each region
options.explanation: Item permission determines access to an item, not which subset of rows appears after it opens.

options.label: Object-level security for the sales table
options.explanation: OLS hides a table or object entirely; Jonas still needs the sales table, filtered to Norway.

options.label: Assign each manager the workspace Viewer role
options.explanation: A workspace role controls access and capabilities, but does not filter rows for each manager in a shared semantic model.

questions.decisiveClue: The requirement is about a different subset of rows after the report opens, which points specifically to RLS.

questions.title: Fresh analysis over large Delta tables
questions.context: Aurora stores large sales tables as Delta tables in OneLake. Marta wants interactive analytics without relying on a traditional full Import refresh before report queries run.
questions.question: Which storage mode most directly fits the scenario?

options.label: Direct Lake
options.explanation: Direct Lake is designed to query required Delta-table columns from OneLake for interactive analytics without the traditional full Import-copy path.

options.label: Import
options.explanation: Import depends on a copied in-memory model refreshed on a schedule, which conflicts with the stated requirement.

options.label: DirectQuery
options.explanation: DirectQuery is a source-query path; the OneLake Delta-table and no-traditional-Import clues point to Direct Lake.

options.label: Live connection
options.explanation: A live connection connects a report to an existing semantic model; it is not the storage mode for these Delta tables.

questions.decisiveClue: The combination of Delta tables in OneLake, interactive analytics, and avoiding a traditional full Import refresh is decisive.

questions.title: Shared customer accounts
questions.context: Some Aurora customers hold several purchasing accounts. Some accounts are shared by several customer entities. Finance needs balances by customer without duplicating balance facts.
questions.question: Which model design fits this requirement?

options.label: Use a CustomerAccount bridge table between Customer and Account
options.explanation: A bridge records the shared associations while preserving each balance fact once.

options.label: Create a direct many-to-many relationship from Customer to FactBalance
options.explanation: This skips the account association and makes filtering harder to reason about.

options.label: Duplicate balance rows once for each linked customer
options.explanation: Duplicating facts would overstate balances when totals are calculated.

options.label: Add bidirectional filters directly between Customer and Account
options.explanation: Filter direction does not model the shared associations or preserve fact grain; the many-to-many relationship still needs a bridge.

questions.decisiveClue: Both sides can have several associations, but the facts must not be duplicated: that is the bridge-table pattern.

questions.title: A retried API call duplicates order lines
questions.context: Aurora’s daily order export occasionally lands the same order line twice because a retried API call resubmitted it. Separately, OrderDate arrives as inconsistent text such as “2026-03-08” and “03/08/2026”.
questions.question: Which operation fixes the retried-call problem specifically, without touching OrderDate values?

options.label: Remove duplicate rows using the order line key
options.explanation: Yes. This removes the repeated record introduced by the retry while leaving other columns untouched.

options.label: Change OrderDate to a date type
options.explanation: This resolves the inconsistent date text, not the duplicated order line.

options.label: Merge queries on OrderID
options.explanation: Merging combines data from another query; it does not remove a row duplicated by a retried call.

options.label: Group by OrderID and sum the line amounts
options.explanation: Grouping only by order collapses legitimate order lines along with duplicates and changes the required row grain.

questions.decisiveClue: A row repeated because of a retried call is a duplicate-row problem, distinct from the separate date-format issue in the same scenario.

questions.title: A repeating loyalty attribute is not a sales fact
questions.context: Aurora’s sales export repeats each customer’s current loyalty tier and its associated discount rate on every order line. For this reporting model, each customer has one current tier, and Marta wants to group revenue by that tier.
questions.question: Where should the loyalty-tier attributes live in the star schema?

options.label: Move them into DimCustomer as customer attributes
options.explanation: Yes. In this model the tier and associated rate describe the customer and repeat across many sales rows, so they belong in the customer dimension.

options.label: Keep them in FactSales next to Revenue
options.explanation: That would repeat descriptive customer attributes on every transaction row and make the model less reusable.

options.label: Turn the discount rate into a DAX measure
options.explanation: The scenario describes a stored customer attribute, not a value that must be calculated from filter context.

options.label: Create calculated columns for the tier and rate in FactSales
options.explanation: Calculated columns in the fact table would still duplicate the customer attributes on every transaction row.

questions.decisiveClue: The tier and rate describe a customer and repeat across that customer’s transaction rows, so they belong on the dimension side of the star schema.

questions.title: Same question, three engines
questions.context: An analyst wants total revenue by region for the last 30 days. The rows live in a Warehouse table. A separate Eventhouse holds device ping counts for the same period, and a semantic model has not been built over either yet.
questions.question: Which language is the closest fit for filtering and aggregating the Warehouse table directly?

options.label: T-SQL
options.explanation: Yes. Warehouse exposes a relational T-SQL endpoint suited to filtering and aggregating its tables directly.

options.label: KQL
options.explanation: KQL is the query language for Eventhouse and Real-Time Intelligence, not the Warehouse’s relational tables.

options.label: DAX
options.explanation: DAX operates over a semantic model’s relationships and filter context; no semantic model exists yet in this scenario.

options.label: Power Query M
options.explanation: Power Query M connects to and transforms data; it is not the direct query language for aggregating a Warehouse table.

questions.decisiveClue: The question asks about querying the Warehouse table directly, before any semantic model or event store is involved.

questions.title: SQL-endpoint security changes the Direct Lake query path
questions.context: Aurora uses a Direct Lake on SQL endpoints semantic model over FactSales. Report queries normally use Direct Lake. A security engineer then defines row-level security on FactSales in the SQL analytics endpoint, and the affected report queries begin using the SQL analytics endpoint instead.
questions.question: What is the most direct explanation for the change in query path?

options.label: Direct Lake falls back to DirectQuery because RLS is defined on the SQL analytics endpoint
options.explanation: Yes. For Direct Lake on SQL endpoints, row-level security defined at the SQL analytics endpoint is a documented condition that causes affected queries to fall back to DirectQuery through that endpoint.

options.label: Direct Lake is broken and needs to be rebuilt
options.explanation: The behavior is a documented fallback for Direct Lake on SQL endpoints, not evidence that the semantic model is damaged.

options.label: The model silently switched to a full Import refresh
options.explanation: The model has not changed to Import mode. The query path has fallen back from Direct Lake to DirectQuery through the SQL analytics endpoint.

options.label: The XMLA endpoint now handles queries because security was enabled
options.explanation: The XMLA endpoint is used to manage and connect to semantic models; it is not the query fallback described here.

questions.decisiveClue: The model is explicitly Direct Lake on SQL endpoints, and RLS was added at that SQL endpoint—the combination that triggers DirectQuery fallback.

questions.title: Late-arriving orders in a rolling window
questions.context: Aurora’s FactSales incremental refresh policy keeps 5 years of history and refreshes only the last 10 days. A distribution partner occasionally reports order corrections up to 20 days after the original sale.
questions.question: What should Priya change so those late corrections are captured without reprocessing all 5 years?

options.label: Increase the refresh (incremental) range to cover at least 20 days
options.explanation: Yes. The refresh range must cover the realistic lateness window, independent of how much history is retained.

options.label: Switch to a full refresh of the whole table on every run
options.explanation: This reprocesses far more than necessary and undermines the purpose of incremental refresh.

options.label: Shorten the historical retention window to 20 days
options.explanation: Retention controls how much history stays in the table; it does not change whether recent late-arriving rows get refreshed.

options.label: Enable DirectQuery for the newest partition only
options.explanation: A real-time partition addresses current incoming data; it does not reprocess corrections made to imported rows 20 days old.

questions.decisiveClue: The refresh range must cover the realistic lateness window, which is a separate policy from historical retention.

questions.title: Ten measures, repeated time intelligence
questions.context: Aurora’s model already defines ten base measures, including Total Sales and Total Cost. Marta now wants a Year-to-Date and Prior-Year version of every one of them, and the modeler wants to avoid writing twenty nearly identical DAX measures.
questions.question: What is the most direct way to add YTD and Prior-Year variants for every base measure?

options.label: Build a calculation group with YTD and Prior-Year calculation items
options.explanation: Yes. A calculation group applies the same time-intelligence pattern across every existing and future base measure without duplicating DAX.

options.label: Duplicate each measure and wrap it in the matching time-intelligence function
options.explanation: This works but multiplies maintenance for every future base measure, which a calculation group is designed to avoid.

options.label: Add a new relationship to a second date-table copy
options.explanation: An extra date-table relationship does not by itself produce YTD or Prior-Year variants.

options.label: Create YTD and Prior-Year visual calculations on every report
options.explanation: Report-level visual calculations duplicate logic across visuals and do not create reusable model-wide variants for every base measure.

questions.decisiveClue: Reusing one time-intelligence pattern across many existing measures without duplicating DAX per measure is the calculation-group scenario.

questions.title: A trusted model for organization-wide reuse
questions.context: Aurora has tested a semantic model against finance controls. The governance team wants people across the organization to recognize it as reliable and authoritative, and only authorized reviewers may grant that status.
questions.question: Which endorsement should the authorized reviewer apply?

options.label: Certified
options.explanation: Certified identifies content that an organization-authorized reviewer has confirmed meets organizational quality standards.

options.label: Promoted
options.explanation: Promotion indicates that an item owner believes content is ready to share, but it does not carry the authorized organizational review described here.

options.label: Master data
options.explanation: Master data designates a data item as a core single source of truth for a business data domain. The scenario asks for organizational quality certification of a reusable analytical model, not a master-data designation.

options.label: Make the model discoverable
options.explanation: Discoverability helps users find metadata, but it does not assert that an authorized reviewer has approved the model's quality.

questions.decisiveClue: The requirement for an organization-authorized reviewer to confirm reliability and quality points to Certified rather than Promoted.

questions.title: A new report inherits protection from its semantic model
questions.context: Aurora applies a Microsoft Purview sensitivity label to a supported Power BI semantic model containing confidential margin data. A new Power BI report is then created from that semantic model through a supported path.
questions.question: What should the governance team expect when the new report is created?

options.label: The new report inherits the semantic model’s sensitivity label
options.explanation: Yes. In a supported Power BI path, a new downstream report inherits the sensitivity label from the labeled semantic model upon creation.

options.label: The report is automatically certified
options.explanation: Certification is a separate endorsement about trust and quality; sensitivity-label inheritance does not certify the report.

options.label: The label grants report access to finance users
options.explanation: Sensitivity labels classify and protect information. They do not grant workspace, item, or semantic-model permissions.

options.label: The label is removed when the report is created
options.explanation: The supported behavior is inheritance upon creation, not automatic removal of the label.

questions.decisiveClue: The report is newly created from an already labeled semantic model through a supported Power BI path, which invokes label inheritance upon creation.

questions.title: Promote content while keeping environment settings separate
questions.context: Aurora promotes Fabric content from Development to Test and Production. The item definition should remain consistent, but each stage must use its own supported data-source or parameter values.
questions.question: Which lifecycle design most directly meets the requirement?

options.label: Use a deployment pipeline with deployment rules for stage-specific data sources or parameters
options.explanation: Yes. Deployment pipelines promote supported content between stages, and deployment rules can apply stage-specific data-source or parameter values.

options.label: Manually recreate every item in each workspace
options.explanation: Manual recreation creates avoidable drift and does not provide a controlled promotion path between environments.

options.label: Store Production connection values in the Development item
options.explanation: Putting Production settings into Development defeats environment isolation and can point development work at the wrong data.

options.label: Use workspace roles to rewrite connections during deployment
options.explanation: Workspace roles control access and capabilities; they do not rewrite an item’s data-source or parameter values during deployment.

questions.decisiveClue: The content definition must be promoted through stages while supported environment-specific data-source or parameter values change by stage.

questions.title: Find trusted data before creating another copy
questions.context: Marta needs an existing customer-data item but does not know which workspace owns it. She wants to search Fabric items, inspect metadata and lineage, and use endorsement signals before requesting access.
questions.question: Where should Marta start?

options.label: OneLake catalog
options.explanation: The OneLake catalog provides centralized discovery, item details, lineage, and governance signals across Fabric items.

options.label: Real-Time hub
options.explanation: Real-Time hub is oriented toward discovering and working with streaming data, not general catalog discovery across Fabric items.

options.label: Monitor hub
options.explanation: Monitor hub tracks job and activity status; it is not the central inventory for discovering reusable data items.

options.label: Create a new lakehouse and copy the customer data
options.explanation: Creating another copy before discovering existing governed items increases duplication and bypasses the stated metadata and lineage needs.

questions.decisiveClue: Searching across workspaces while inspecting metadata, lineage, and trust signals is the OneLake catalog use case.

questions.title: Enrich sales without losing unknown customers
questions.context: Aurora is enriching FactSales with customer attributes. Some valid sales rows have a CustomerKey that is not yet present in DimCustomer, and finance must retain every sales row while data quality is investigated.
questions.question: Starting from FactSales, which join behavior preserves the required rows?

options.label: Left outer join from FactSales to DimCustomer
options.explanation: A left outer join retains every FactSales row and adds matching customer attributes when they exist.

options.label: Inner join
options.explanation: An inner join drops sales rows whose customer key has no matching dimension row, violating the retention requirement.

options.label: Right outer join from FactSales to DimCustomer
options.explanation: A right outer join prioritizes retaining all customer rows rather than all sales rows.

options.label: Left anti join
options.explanation: A left anti join returns only unmatched sales rows, which is useful for investigation but not for producing the complete enriched result.

questions.decisiveClue: FactSales is the starting table and every one of its rows must survive whether or not a customer match exists.

questions.title: Reuse external lake data without another copy
questions.context: Aurora already stores curated product files in an external cloud data lake. The analytics team wants those files available from a Fabric lakehouse, but governance does not want another physical copy or a recurring copy job.
questions.question: What should Priya create?

options.label: A OneLake shortcut to the existing data
options.explanation: A OneLake shortcut points to data in another supported storage location so Fabric can use it without creating another edge copy.

options.label: A pipeline that copies the files into the lakehouse every hour
options.explanation: A copy pipeline creates and maintains another physical copy, which conflicts with the stated requirement.

options.label: An Import semantic model over the files
options.explanation: Import mode copies data into a semantic model and does not make the external files themselves available as lakehouse data.

options.label: A scheduled export from the source into CSV files in OneLake
options.explanation: A scheduled export creates another staged copy and adds synchronization work that the scenario explicitly wants to avoid.

questions.decisiveClue: The decisive requirement is to expose existing data through Fabric without copying it; OneLake shortcuts are pointers rather than duplicate storage.

questions.title: Find an existing organizational data stream
questions.context: Aurora receives continuous checkout events. Marta knows another team already publishes the stream in Fabric, but she does not know which workspace owns it and wants to discover streaming data she is permitted to use.
questions.question: Where should Marta start?

options.label: Real-Time hub
options.explanation: Real-Time hub is the tenant-wide place for discovering, ingesting, managing, and consuming streaming data that the user has access to.

options.label: OneLake catalog only
options.explanation: OneLake catalog is the broader Fabric data catalog, but the scenario specifically asks for discovery of streaming data, which is the Real-Time hub use case.

options.label: Monitor hub
options.explanation: Monitor hub is for monitoring Fabric activities and jobs, not for discovering organizational streaming sources.

options.label: Create a new workspace and ingest a duplicate stream
options.explanation: Creating another stream does not address discovery and can introduce unnecessary duplication.

questions.decisiveClue: The asset to discover is a continuous organizational stream, which points specifically to Real-Time hub.

questions.title: Reuse Eventhouse data through OneLake
questions.context: Aurora keeps high-volume device telemetry in a KQL database in an Eventhouse. A downstream team now needs the same data in Delta Lake form so it can be used by other Fabric engines and a Direct Lake semantic model without building a separate export pipeline.
questions.question: Which configuration most directly meets the requirement?

options.label: Enable OneLake availability for the KQL database or required tables
options.explanation: OneLake availability exposes Eventhouse KQL data in Delta Lake format so other Fabric engines, including Power BI Direct Lake, can access it.

options.label: Schedule recurring CSV exports from Eventhouse to a lakehouse
options.explanation: Exports create a second data movement process and are unnecessary when OneLake availability can expose the data directly in Delta form.

options.label: Import the telemetry into a semantic model and use that as the shared store
options.explanation: A semantic model is an analytical layer, not a general Delta Lake representation for other Fabric engines.

options.label: Copy every Eventhouse table into a Warehouse before any other engine uses it
options.explanation: A Warehouse copy is not required merely to make Eventhouse data available in OneLake to other Fabric engines.

questions.decisiveClue: The requirement is to expose existing Eventhouse data as Delta Lake data in OneLake for reuse by other engines without a separate export pipeline.

questions.title: Aggregate Warehouse data without writing SQL
questions.context: A finance analyst needs to join two Warehouse tables, filter the current quarter, and group revenue by region. The analyst wants a graphical no-code experience and does not need to modify stored data.
questions.question: Which Fabric experience is the closest fit?

options.label: Visual Query Editor
options.explanation: The Visual Query Editor provides a no-code graphical experience for read-only querying, including joins, filters, and grouping.

options.label: SQL query editor
options.explanation: The SQL query editor can perform the analysis, but it requires writing T-SQL and therefore does not meet the stated no-code preference.

options.label: KQL queryset
options.explanation: KQL is designed for KQL database data and is not the graphical query experience for these Warehouse tables.

options.label: DAX query view
options.explanation: DAX queries operate against a semantic model; the requirement is to query Warehouse tables graphically before a semantic model is involved.

questions.decisiveClue: The workload is read-only Warehouse analysis and the explicit requirement is a graphical no-code query experience.

questions.title: A visual query cannot update Warehouse rows
questions.context: Priya builds a query in the Visual Query Editor and then tries to update incorrect status values in a Warehouse table. The visual query can read and shape the rows, but it cannot execute the required UPDATE statement.
questions.question: What should Priya do?

options.label: Use the SQL query editor and execute the supported T-SQL update there
options.explanation: The Visual Query Editor is limited to read-only DQL/SELECT operations, while the SQL query editor supports DML statements such as UPDATE.

options.label: Add another visual-query transformation that overwrites the source rows
options.explanation: Visual query transformations shape query results; they do not turn the read-only visual query into a DML operation against the source table.

options.label: Run a DAX query that changes the Warehouse rows
options.explanation: DAX queries read and analyze semantic models; they do not update rows in a Warehouse table.

options.label: Run a KQL summarize query against the Warehouse
options.explanation: KQL aggregation does not provide DML updates to a Warehouse table and targets a different query engine.

questions.decisiveClue: The required operation is UPDATE, while the Visual Query Editor supports only read-only DQL/SELECT operations.

questions.title: Give a customer dimension a warehouse key
questions.context: Aurora integrates customers from multiple source systems. Source customer identifiers are meaningful in those systems and can differ in format. The dimensional model needs a compact, stable key to identify each dimension row independently of source-system identifiers.
questions.question: What should the modeler add to DimCustomer?

options.label: A surrogate key
options.explanation: A surrogate key gives each dimension row an independent warehouse identifier and is the recommended key pattern for dimensions.

options.label: A revenue measure
options.explanation: Revenue is a fact measurement and does not provide a stable identifier for dimension rows.

options.label: Use only the source customer identifier as the dimension key
options.explanation: Relying only on a natural source key couples the warehouse dimension to source-system key semantics and does not meet the independent-key requirement.

options.label: A report-side row number calculated in Power BI
options.explanation: A report-side row number is not a persistent warehouse dimension key and cannot reliably serve fact-table relationships during ETL.

questions.decisiveClue: The dimension needs a warehouse-controlled identifier that is independent of meaningful source-system keys.

questions.title: Keep a fact when its dimension member is not known yet
questions.context: Aurora loads sales facts after dimension processing. A valid sale arrives with a ProductCode that cannot yet be matched to DimProduct. The fact table design requires ProductKey to remain NOT NULL, and finance must keep the sale while the source issue is investigated.
questions.question: What is the best dimensional-modeling treatment?

options.label: Map the fact to a designated Unknown member in DimProduct
options.explanation: A special dimension member can represent unknown or missing dimension states while preserving the fact and keeping the dimension key populated.

options.label: Store NULL in ProductKey
options.explanation: The scenario explicitly requires ProductKey to remain NOT NULL, and a null key also prevents the fact from resolving to a dimension member.

options.label: Discard the sale until the product appears
options.explanation: Dropping a valid business event loses facts and violates the requirement to retain the sale.

options.label: Create a new real product row using guessed attributes
options.explanation: Inventing a real product member introduces false master data. A designated Unknown member represents the unresolved state explicitly.

questions.decisiveClue: The sale is valid and must be retained, but its dimension key cannot be null; a designated Unknown dimension member satisfies both constraints.

questions.title: Resolve dimension members before loading facts
questions.context: Aurora’s nightly warehouse load must add new customers and then load the day’s sales facts. Each sales fact needs the correct customer surrogate key when it is inserted.
questions.question: Which load order is most appropriate?

options.label: Process DimCustomer before FactSales
options.explanation: Dimension tables should be processed before dependent facts so new members and their surrogate keys are available when facts are loaded.

options.label: Load FactSales first and process DimCustomer afterward
options.explanation: Loading the facts first can leave new facts without the dimension members and surrogate keys they need.

options.label: Load both in parallel and ignore unresolved keys
options.explanation: Ignoring the dependency can produce unresolved dimension references and weakens the integrity of the dimensional load.

options.label: Refresh the semantic model before loading either table
options.explanation: Refreshing the semantic model does not create the missing warehouse dimension members and should occur only after the underlying data is ready.

questions.decisiveClue: Fact rows require surrogate keys from newly processed dimension members, so the dependent dimension must be loaded first.

questions.title: Load the fact table at the required analytical grain
questions.context: Aurora receives individual scanner events for every item movement. The approved warehouse requirement is daily inventory movement by Store, Product, and Date; event identifiers and event-level timestamps are not needed for any downstream analysis.
questions.question: Which transformation best aligns the fact table with the approved grain?

options.label: Aggregate the source events by Store, Product, and Date before loading the fact table
options.explanation: Aggregation can raise the grain of a fact table when lower-level event detail is not required, reducing rows while preserving the required dimensions and measures.

options.label: Load every scanner event and call the table daily-grain
options.explanation: Keeping event-level identifiers and timestamps preserves event grain, so the resulting fact table would not actually be at the stated daily grain.

options.label: Move each scanner event into DimProduct
options.explanation: Scanner events are business observations, not descriptive product attributes, so they do not belong in a product dimension.

options.label: Remove duplicate-looking events without grouping the measures
options.explanation: Deduplication addresses repeated records; it does not intentionally aggregate legitimate events to the required daily analytical grain.

questions.decisiveClue: The required grain is explicitly Store × Product × Date and no event-level analysis is needed, so legitimate lower-level events should be aggregated to that grain.

questions.title: Create a reusable Warehouse view
questions.context: Aurora needs a reusable SQL view that joins sales and store data in a Fabric Warehouse. The developer wants to create the view directly in the Fabric portal.
questions.question: Which editor should the developer use?

options.label: SQL query editor
options.explanation: Creating a view requires a DDL statement such as CREATE VIEW, which belongs in the SQL query editor.

options.label: Visual Query Editor only
options.explanation: The Visual Query Editor is limited to read-only DQL/SELECT execution and does not support DDL statements such as CREATE VIEW.

options.label: DAX query view
options.explanation: DAX query view works with a semantic model and does not create SQL views in a Warehouse.

options.label: KQL queryset
options.explanation: A KQL queryset queries a KQL database; it does not create a T-SQL view in a Fabric Warehouse.

questions.decisiveClue: CREATE VIEW is a DDL operation against the Warehouse, which requires the SQL query editor rather than the read-only visual query path.

questions.title: Summarize telemetry into time buckets
questions.context: Aurora stores device pings in an Eventhouse KQL database. An analyst needs a query that counts pings in fixed five-minute time buckets before any semantic model is created.
questions.question: Which approach most directly fits the data and requirement?

options.label: Use KQL with summarize and bin()
options.explanation: KQL is the native query language for KQL database data, and summarize with bin() is designed for grouped time-bucket aggregations.

options.label: Use a DAX measure in a semantic model
options.explanation: No semantic model exists yet, and DAX is not the direct query language for the Eventhouse KQL table.

options.label: Use Power Query M as the Eventhouse query language
options.explanation: Power Query can transform data in supported ingestion workflows, but M is not the native query language for querying the KQL database directly.

options.label: Use the Warehouse Visual Query Editor
options.explanation: The scenario data is in a KQL database, not a Warehouse or SQL analytics endpoint targeted by the Warehouse Visual Query Editor.

questions.decisiveClue: The rows are in an Eventhouse KQL database and the task is a direct time-bucket aggregation, matching KQL summarize/bin semantics.

questions.title: Keep RLS effective for a workspace consumer
questions.context: Aurora has RLS roles on a sales semantic model. Erik needs to open and interact with reports directly in the workspace, but he must remain subject to those RLS filters and must not edit workspace content.
questions.question: Which workspace role is the best fit?

options.label: Viewer
options.explanation: The Viewer role is the workspace role intended for consumers and is the role to use when RLS must remain enforced for users browsing workspace content.

options.label: Contributor
options.explanation: Contributors have write capabilities. Users with semantic-model Write permission are not constrained by RLS in the same way as read-only consumers.

options.label: Member
options.explanation: Member grants broader workspace management and write capabilities than a report consumer needs and is not the least-privilege choice for enforcing RLS.

options.label: Admin
options.explanation: Admin grants full workspace management and is far beyond the requirement for a read-only report consumer.

questions.decisiveClue: The user is a report consumer who must browse workspace content while remaining subject to RLS, which points to the Viewer role.

questions.title: Let an analyst build from a governed semantic model
questions.context: Aurora keeps its certified Finance semantic model in a central workspace. Nina can consume existing reports, and governance now wants her to create a new report in another workspace using that same semantic model without granting her permission to modify the model.
questions.question: Which semantic-model permission is specifically required for the new authoring scenario?

options.label: Build
options.explanation: Build permission allows a user to create new content from a semantic model without granting model Write permission.

options.label: Write
options.explanation: Write would allow modification of the semantic model itself and is more privilege than the scenario requires.

options.label: Reshare
options.explanation: Reshare controls whether the user can grant model access to others; it is not the permission that enables creation of new reports from the model.

options.label: Workspace Admin
options.explanation: Workspace Admin is a broad workspace role and is unnecessary for reusing a shared semantic model in another workspace.

questions.decisiveClue: The analyst must create new content from an existing semantic model but must not modify that model; that is the purpose of Build permission.

questions.title: Grant access to one folder in a lakehouse
questions.context: Aurora stores several unstructured finance folders in one lakehouse. An audit group should be able to read only the /Files/PublishedAudit folder and should not gain access to the other folders in the item.
questions.question: Which control most directly implements this requirement?

options.label: A OneLake security role that grants access to the specific folder
options.explanation: OneLake table and folder security can grant access to selected folders within a data item, providing file-level scope without opening the whole lakehouse.

options.label: Workspace Viewer access to the lakehouse workspace
options.explanation: Workspace access is broader than the requested folder-level scope and does not by itself express access to only one folder.

options.label: RLS on a downstream semantic model
options.explanation: Semantic-model RLS filters rows in model tables; it does not grant or deny access to an unstructured OneLake folder.

options.label: A sensitivity label on the folder name
options.explanation: Sensitivity labeling classifies and protects information but is not the folder-selection permission mechanism described in OneLake security.

questions.decisiveClue: The security boundary is a specific folder of unstructured OneLake data, so table/folder security in a OneLake security role is the matching control.

questions.title: Apply the same source restrictions across Fabric engines
questions.context: Aurora wants contractors to see only Region = "NO" rows and never see the Cost column in a lakehouse table. The contractors are not workspace Admins, Members, or Contributors. The restrictions must follow the source data when they use supported Fabric engines such as SQL, Spark, and Direct Lake on OneLake.
questions.question: Where should Aurora define the source-level restrictions?

options.label: In a OneLake security role with row-level and column-level rules
options.explanation: OneLake security can define granular row and column access on the source data and enforce those permissions across supported Fabric analytics experiences.

options.label: As hidden filters in each Power BI report
options.explanation: Report filters affect only those report experiences and do not secure the underlying lakehouse data for SQL or Spark access.

options.label: By making the contractors Contributors and relying on workspace permissions
options.explanation: Contributor is a write-capable workspace role and OneLake row/column controls do not restrict Admin, Member, or Contributor users as ordinary consumers.

options.label: By certifying the lakehouse
options.explanation: Certification signals trust and quality; it does not define which rows or columns a user can read.

questions.decisiveClue: The restrictions must live with the lakehouse source and remain effective across multiple Fabric engines for non-write workspace users, which is the OneLake security role use case.

questions.title: Hide a sensitive model column and its metadata
questions.context: Aurora has one HR semantic model. Most analysts may use employee department and headcount, but they must not be able to see or discover the Salary column in the model metadata. HR managers can use the full model.
questions.question: Which semantic-model control best fits the requirement?

options.label: Object-level security that denies access to the Salary column
options.explanation: OLS can hide model tables or columns and their metadata for users assigned to the secured role.

options.label: Row-level security on Employee
options.explanation: RLS filters which rows are visible; it does not make a sensitive column disappear from the model schema.

options.label: Hide the Salary column from report view
options.explanation: Hiding a field is a modeling convenience, not a security boundary; authorized model access can still expose it.

options.label: Assign all analysts the Viewer workspace role
options.explanation: Viewer reduces workspace capabilities, but it does not by itself hide one semantic-model column from users who can query the model.

questions.decisiveClue: The requirement is to make one model column and its metadata unavailable while retaining the rest of the model, which is OLS rather than row filtering.

questions.title: Version Fabric workspace items in Git
questions.context: Aurora’s analytics developers want supported Fabric items in a development workspace tracked in source control so they can commit changes, review history, collaborate through branches, and update the workspace from the repository.
questions.question: Which Fabric capability is designed for this workflow?

options.label: Fabric Git integration
options.explanation: Fabric Git integration connects source control at the workspace level and supports committing workspace changes and updating the workspace from the connected Git branch.

options.label: Deployment pipeline only
options.explanation: Deployment pipelines promote content between lifecycle stages; they are not a replacement for repository version history and branch-based source control.

options.label: Lineage view
options.explanation: Lineage shows dependencies and data flow between items; it does not provide commits, branches, or version history.

options.label: Certification
options.explanation: Certification marks trusted content; it is unrelated to source-control history.

questions.decisiveClue: The explicit requirements are commits, version history, branches, and synchronizing a development workspace with a repository.

questions.title: Store Power BI development artifacts as text files
questions.context: Aurora wants report and semantic-model definitions to be reviewable in Git as separate human-readable files instead of treating one binary PBIX file as the primary source artifact. The team still authors in Power BI Desktop.
questions.question: Which project format best supports this workflow?

options.label: Power BI Project (PBIP)
options.explanation: PBIP saves report and semantic-model definitions into a source-control-friendly folder structure of text files designed for Git and CI/CD workflows.

options.label: PBIX only
options.explanation: PBIX is the standard packaged Desktop file, but it does not provide the same decomposed text-file project structure requested for source-control review.

options.label: PBIT
options.explanation: PBIT is a reusable report template without data; it is not the source-control-oriented project format for decomposed report and model definitions.

options.label: PBIDS
options.explanation: PBIDS describes a single data-source connection to streamline Get Data; it does not store report and semantic-model project definitions.

questions.decisiveClue: The team specifically needs report and semantic-model definitions decomposed into human-readable files for Git-based development.

questions.title: Find downstream dependencies outside the current workspace
questions.context: Aurora plans to change a shared semantic model. Its workspace lineage view shows the local dependencies, but the owner must also identify reports and other downstream items that depend on the model from different workspaces before making a breaking change.
questions.question: What should the owner use for the cross-workspace downstream check?

options.label: Impact analysis for the semantic model
options.explanation: Lineage view does not show downstream items in other workspaces; impact analysis is the appropriate way to investigate those downstream dependencies.

options.label: Only the current workspace lineage view
options.explanation: Lineage view shows connections in the current workspace and one-step upstream external sources, but not downstream items in other workspaces.

options.label: Git commit history
options.explanation: Git history can show source changes, but it does not enumerate live downstream Fabric dependencies across workspaces.

options.label: Monitor hub
options.explanation: Monitor hub tracks activity and job status rather than the downstream dependency graph needed before a breaking change.

questions.decisiveClue: The missing dependencies are downstream and located in other workspaces, exactly the limitation for which impact analysis is needed.

questions.title: Modify semantic-model metadata through XMLA
questions.context: Aurora manages a semantic model on a supported Fabric capacity with an external tabular-model tool. The tool can connect and query the model, but the team now needs it to deploy metadata changes and run management operations through the XMLA endpoint.
questions.question: What capability must be available for those write operations?

options.label: XMLA endpoint read-write, together with the required model permissions
options.explanation: Read-only XMLA allows querying, while metadata scripting, deployment, and other write-management operations require XMLA read-write and appropriate permissions.

options.label: XMLA endpoint read-only
options.explanation: Read-only is sufficient for querying and browsing but not for deploying or scripting metadata changes.

options.label: Build permission alone, with XMLA left read-only
options.explanation: Build can enable read access through XMLA, but it does not turn a read-only endpoint into a write-capable management endpoint.

options.label: A deployment-pipeline data-source rule
options.explanation: Deployment rules control supported stage-specific configuration; they do not enable an external tool to write semantic-model metadata through XMLA.

questions.decisiveClue: The tool already reads the model; the new requirement is to deploy or script metadata, which changes the XMLA requirement from read-only to read-write.

questions.title: Distribute a reusable report starting point without data
questions.context: Aurora wants regional analysts to start new Power BI reports with the same pages, visuals, model definition, and query definitions, but the distributed file must not contain imported business data. Analysts will supply parameters and connect with their own credentials.
questions.question: Which reusable artifact best fits?

options.label: A Power BI template (.PBIT)
options.explanation: A PBIT can preserve report layout, model definitions, and queries while excluding the report data, making it a reusable starting point.

options.label: A populated PBIX file
options.explanation: A PBIX can contain imported data, which conflicts with the requirement that the distributed starting artifact contain no business data.

options.label: A PBIDS file
options.explanation: PBIDS streamlines connection to one data source but does not carry the report pages, visuals, model, and query definitions requested.

options.label: A CSV export of the report data
options.explanation: A CSV contains data rather than the reusable report and model definitions the team wants to standardize.

questions.decisiveClue: The artifact must preserve the report/model/query starting structure while containing no imported data, which is the defining PBIT scenario.

questions.title: Give report authors a standardized Get Data entry point
questions.context: Aurora wants beginner report authors to open a small file that points Power BI Desktop to one approved data source. When opened, authors should be prompted for credentials and then choose tables in Navigator instead of manually finding and configuring the source each time.
questions.question: Which artifact is designed for this?

options.label: A PBIDS file
options.explanation: PBIDS files specify a single Power BI Desktop data source and streamline Get Data by prompting for credentials and opening Navigator.

options.label: A PBIT file
options.explanation: PBIT is a broader reusable report template containing report/model/query definitions; the scenario only needs a standardized data-source connection entry point.

options.label: A PBIP project
options.explanation: PBIP decomposes report and model definitions for development and source control; it is not the lightweight single-data-source connection file described.

options.label: A deployment pipeline
options.explanation: Deployment pipelines move supported Fabric content between lifecycle stages; they do not give Desktop authors a one-file Get Data connection entry point.

questions.decisiveClue: The requested file does one job: describe one approved data source so Desktop can prompt for credentials and open Navigator.

questions.title: Reuse one governed model across many reports
questions.context: Aurora has one certified enterprise Sales semantic model with governed measures and RLS. Several teams need to build their own reports in separate workspaces, but governance does not want each team to copy and independently maintain the model.
questions.question: Which design best preserves the governed model as the single reusable analytical layer?

options.label: Grant appropriate users Build permission and create reports connected to the shared semantic model
options.explanation: Reports can be built across workspaces on the existing semantic model without copying it, preserving central measures and security such as RLS.

options.label: Copy the semantic model into every reporting workspace
options.explanation: Copies create multiple model definitions that can drift and require separate governance and maintenance.

options.label: Export the model data to files for each team to import independently
options.explanation: Independent imports duplicate data/model logic and break the stated goal of one governed reusable analytical layer.

options.label: Make every report author an Admin of the semantic-model workspace
options.explanation: Workspace Admin is excessive privilege and is not required merely to build reports from a shared semantic model.

questions.decisiveClue: The same governed measures and RLS must serve reports in several workspaces without model copies, which calls for a shared semantic model plus Build permission.

questions.title: Let readers switch the field used by a visual
questions.context: Aurora has one chart that should let report readers choose whether the axis shows Product, Region, or Channel by selecting from a slicer. The modeler wants the visual to change fields without maintaining several duplicate charts.
questions.question: Which modeling feature is designed for this?

options.label: A field parameter
options.explanation: Field parameters let report readers dynamically switch the dimensions or measures used by visuals, commonly through a slicer.

options.label: A calculation group
options.explanation: Calculation groups apply reusable calculation logic to measures; they are not primarily for letting readers swap the dimension placed on a visual axis.

options.label: Row-level security
options.explanation: RLS changes which rows a user may see; it does not let a reader choose which field a visual analyzes.

options.label: A bookmark for every field choice
options.explanation: Bookmarks can capture report states, but maintaining separate bookmark-driven chart states is not the model feature designed for dynamic field selection.

questions.decisiveClue: The requirement is for a reader-controlled slicer that swaps dimensions or measures used by the same visual.

questions.title: Change currency display without converting the measure to text
questions.context: Aurora has one numeric Revenue measure. Depending on the selected market, it should display with the appropriate currency format, but the measure must stay numeric so charts can aggregate and scale it correctly.
questions.question: Which approach best meets both requirements?

options.label: Apply a dynamic format string to the Revenue measure
options.explanation: Dynamic format strings can change how a measure is displayed by context while preserving the measure’s numeric data type.

options.label: Return FORMAT([Revenue], ...) from the Revenue measure
options.explanation: FORMAT returns text, which can prevent visuals that require numeric values from treating the result as a number.

options.label: Create a separate text measure for every market and replace Revenue
options.explanation: This multiplies measures and still turns the display values into text rather than preserving one reusable numeric measure.

options.label: Use a field parameter to change the number format
options.explanation: Field parameters switch fields used in analysis; they do not define a context-dependent numeric format string for one measure.

questions.decisiveClue: The display must vary by context while Revenue remains numeric; dynamic format strings solve the text-conversion problem created by FORMAT().

questions.title: Sum an expression evaluated for every sales row
questions.context: FactSales stores Quantity and UnitPrice but has no persisted LineRevenue column. Marta needs a Total Revenue measure that multiplies Quantity by UnitPrice for each visible fact row and then sums those row results.
questions.question: Which DAX pattern most directly fits the calculation?

options.label: SUMX(FactSales, FactSales[Quantity] * FactSales[UnitPrice])
options.explanation: SUMX is an iterator: it evaluates the expression for each row of the table and then sums the row-level results.

options.label: SUM(FactSales[Quantity]) * SUM(FactSales[UnitPrice])
options.explanation: Multiplying two independent column totals is not equivalent to summing Quantity × UnitPrice for each transaction row.

options.label: COUNTROWS(FactSales)
options.explanation: COUNTROWS returns the number of visible rows and does not evaluate the required row-level revenue expression.

options.label: SELECTEDVALUE(FactSales[Quantity]) * SELECTEDVALUE(FactSales[UnitPrice])
options.explanation: SELECTEDVALUE is intended for a context with one distinct value and does not iterate over all visible sales rows.

questions.decisiveClue: The required measure must evaluate Quantity × UnitPrice separately for each fact row before adding the results, which requires an iterator such as SUMX.

questions.title: Avoid recalculating the same DAX expression
questions.context: Aurora’s year-over-year percentage measure evaluates the same prior-year sales expression twice: once in the numerator and again in the denominator. The formula is correct, but Marta wants to reduce repeated evaluation and make it easier to read and debug.
questions.question: What is the best first change?

options.label: Evaluate prior-year sales once in a VAR and reuse that variable in RETURN
options.explanation: A DAX variable can store the result of an expression once and reuse it, improving readability and potentially reducing repeated evaluation work.

options.label: Duplicate the prior-year expression a third time in a helper branch
options.explanation: Repeating the same expression adds complexity and can increase evaluation work rather than reducing it.

options.label: Move the entire year-over-year calculation into a FactSales calculated column
options.explanation: Year-over-year logic depends on filter context and is naturally a measure; moving it to a row-level calculated column changes the calculation semantics.

options.label: Wrap both repeated expressions in FORMAT()
options.explanation: FORMAT changes presentation and returns text; it does not address repeated evaluation of the prior-year calculation.

questions.decisiveClue: The identical expensive expression is reused within one measure, which is the classic case for calculating it once in a DAX variable.

questions.title: Prepare a semantic model to grow beyond standard size limits
questions.context: Aurora has a semantic model on a supported Fabric capacity. After future refreshes, the compressed model is expected to grow well beyond the standard model-size limit and potentially beyond 10 GB. The team also uses XMLA-based management tools.
questions.question: Which model configuration is most relevant?

options.label: Enable Large semantic model storage format
options.explanation: Large semantic model storage format allows supported-capacity models to exceed the default size limit, is required for models to grow beyond 10 GB, and can also improve XMLA write performance.

options.label: Convert every table to DirectQuery regardless of workload requirements
options.explanation: DirectQuery can avoid imported model size, but converting every table changes query behavior and is not required simply because supported large-model storage exists.

options.label: Export the semantic model as a PBIT template
options.explanation: PBIT is a reusable report template format and does not change the capacity storage format or size limits of the published semantic model.

options.label: Assign users the Viewer role
options.explanation: Workspace roles affect access, not semantic-model storage limits or XMLA write storage format.

questions.decisiveClue: The model must grow past the normal imported-model size boundary on supported capacity and may exceed 10 GB, which is the Large semantic model storage format scenario.

questions.title: Determine why one report visual is slow
questions.context: Users report that one Aurora matrix takes several seconds to react to a slicer. The modeler needs to determine whether the delay is mainly the visual’s DAX query, a DirectQuery source request, or rendering the visual itself before deciding what to optimize.
questions.question: Which tool should the modeler use first?

options.label: Performance Analyzer
options.explanation: Performance Analyzer records visual load time and breaks it into categories such as DAX query, DirectQuery, visual display, and other work.

options.label: Lineage view
options.explanation: Lineage shows dependencies between items but does not break a visual interaction into query and rendering durations.

options.label: Deployment pipeline comparison
options.explanation: Deployment pipelines compare and promote lifecycle stages; they do not profile report visual execution time.

options.label: Endorsement metadata
options.explanation: Endorsement communicates trust in an item and provides no performance timing diagnostics.

questions.decisiveClue: The immediate question is which component of a single visual’s load time is slow, and Performance Analyzer exposes exactly that timing breakdown.

questions.title: Filter a measure with a row-by-row expression
questions.context: Aurora needs a measure for revenue from high-value sales lines only. A line qualifies when Quantity × UnitPrice exceeds 1,000, and there is no stored LineRevenue column. The filter therefore must evaluate an expression for each visible FactSales row before the Revenue measure is calculated.
questions.question: Which DAX approach best matches that requirement?

options.label: Use FILTER(FactSales, FactSales[Quantity] * FactSales[UnitPrice] > 1000) as a table filter in CALCULATE
options.explanation: FILTER returns the subset of FactSales rows for which the row-level expression is true, and CALCULATE can evaluate Revenue in that resulting filter context.

options.label: Filter only FactSales[Quantity] > 1000
options.explanation: The qualification depends on Quantity multiplied by UnitPrice, so filtering Quantity alone implements a different business rule.

options.label: Use FORMAT([Revenue], "#,##0") inside CALCULATE
options.explanation: FORMAT controls display and returns text; it does not construct the row subset defined by the high-value line condition.

options.label: Use ALL(FactSales) with no qualifying predicate
options.explanation: ALL removes filters; by itself it does not retain only rows where Quantity × UnitPrice exceeds the threshold.

questions.decisiveClue: The qualifying condition is a row-level expression over two columns rather than a stored Boolean or single-column filter, so a table-filter expression is needed.

questions.title: Define a running window over ordered periods
questions.context: Aurora needs a calculation that, for each month shown in a visual, identifies the ordered set of months from the start of the current year through the current month so those rows can be iterated to produce a running total.
questions.question: Which DAX function is specifically designed to return that relative or absolute window of rows?

options.label: WINDOW
options.explanation: WINDOW returns a set of rows positioned by absolute or relative boundaries in an ordered relation, making it suitable for window-based calculations such as running totals.

options.label: SELECTEDVALUE
options.explanation: SELECTEDVALUE returns one scalar value when a single distinct value is in context; it does not return an ordered range of rows.

options.label: FORMAT
options.explanation: FORMAT converts a value to formatted text and does not define an ordered row window.

options.label: RELATED
options.explanation: RELATED follows a relationship to retrieve a value from another table; it does not construct a running window of periods.

questions.decisiveClue: The calculation needs a set of ordered rows bounded from the start of a partition to the current row, which is exactly the purpose of DAX window functions.

questions.title: Inspect measure metadata with DAX
questions.context: Before refactoring Aurora’s enterprise model, Marta wants a DAX query that returns a table listing model measures together with metadata such as their names, home tables, descriptions, and expressions.
questions.question: Which function family is intended for this kind of semantic-model metadata query?

options.label: INFO.VIEW functions such as INFO.VIEW.MEASURES()
options.explanation: INFO.VIEW functions expose semantic-model metadata as tables that can be queried with DAX, including measure definitions and related properties.

options.label: Iterator functions such as SUMX
options.explanation: SUMX evaluates a numeric expression over table rows; it does not return the model’s measure metadata.

options.label: Time-intelligence functions such as DATEADD
options.explanation: Time-intelligence functions alter date context for calculations; they do not enumerate semantic-model objects.

options.label: FORMAT
options.explanation: FORMAT changes a scalar value to text and does not expose the catalog of measures or their expressions.

questions.decisiveClue: The requested result is metadata about semantic-model objects rather than business data, which points to the DAX information-function family.

questions.title: Choose Dual for a shared composite-model dimension
questions.context: Aurora has a composite model where FactSales is DirectQuery against a relational source. DimProduct comes from the same source, is used heavily in slicers, and also needs to participate efficiently in queries that combine it with the DirectQuery fact table.
questions.question: Which storage mode is the strongest candidate for DimProduct?

options.label: Dual
options.explanation: A dimension in Dual mode can be served from the in-memory cache for suitable queries while acting as DirectQuery when needed with a DirectQuery fact table from the same source.

options.label: DirectQuery only
options.explanation: DirectQuery can work, but it gives up the ability to satisfy suitable dimension-only queries from the imported cache that Dual provides.

options.label: Import only
options.explanation: Import can make slicers fast, but in this composite pattern Dual is specifically designed to let a dimension participate efficiently with a same-source DirectQuery fact as well as cached queries.

options.label: Live connection
options.explanation: Live connection is not a table storage-mode choice for one dimension inside this composite model.

questions.decisiveClue: The table is a shared dimension from the same source as a DirectQuery fact and must support both cached dimension queries and efficient fact queries, which is the Dual pattern.

questions.title: Extend a governed semantic model with local data
questions.context: Marta starts with a live connection to Aurora’s governed Sales semantic model. She now needs to add a small imported Targets table from Excel and create local relationships and measures, while continuing to query the enterprise Sales tables from the published model.
questions.question: Which design enables this extension?

options.label: Add a local model, converting the remote semantic-model connection to DirectQuery and creating a composite model with the imported Targets table
options.explanation: Adding a local model allows the report to extend a remote Power BI semantic model through DirectQuery and combine it with local Import or DirectQuery tables in a composite model.

options.label: Keep the pure live connection and import Targets into that same live model
options.explanation: A pure live connection has no local model to host the imported table, relationships, and local model objects requested.

options.label: Export and copy the entire enterprise semantic model into the report file
options.explanation: Copying the governed model defeats centralized reuse and is unnecessary because composite models can extend the remote model.

options.label: Create a field parameter for the Excel file
options.explanation: Field parameters switch model fields in visuals; they do not add a new data source or create a local composite model.

questions.decisiveClue: The report must keep querying the central semantic model while adding local imported data and relationships, which requires a local model and therefore a composite model.

questions.title: Expose a Direct Lake snapshot only after ETL completes
questions.context: Aurora’s nightly ETL updates several Delta tables over 20 minutes. Finance requires reports to continue showing the previous consistent snapshot until the entire ETL finishes; it must not expose partially updated tables as changes arrive. The Direct Lake model currently has Keep your Direct Lake data up to date enabled.
questions.question: What should Priya change?

options.label: Disable automatic Direct Lake updates and trigger a semantic-model refresh after the ETL completes
options.explanation: A Direct Lake refresh performs framing. Disabling automatic updates lets the team control when the point-in-time baseline advances, so one refresh after ETL exposes the completed state.

options.label: Increase automatic page refresh frequency
options.explanation: Page refresh causes report pages to query again; it does not control the Direct Lake framing baseline or prevent partial ETL states from becoming visible.

options.label: Convert the model to Import solely to delay visibility
options.explanation: Import is not required. Direct Lake framing already provides point-in-time control when automatic updates are disabled and refresh is coordinated with ETL completion.

options.label: Force DirectQuery fallback during the ETL
options.explanation: DirectQuery fallback can return the latest source state and therefore works against the requirement to hold consumers on the previous consistent framed state.

questions.decisiveClue: The key requirement is point-in-time consistency across a multi-table ETL, so the framing event must be deliberately delayed until the ETL has completed.

questions.title: Choose the Direct Lake architecture for a new model
questions.context: Aurora is creating a new Direct Lake semantic model. It needs Direct Lake tables from more than one supported OneLake source, wants OneLake security to govern source access across Fabric engines, and does not want queries silently falling back to DirectQuery through a SQL analytics endpoint.
questions.question: Which Direct Lake option best matches those requirements?

options.label: Direct Lake on OneLake
options.explanation: Direct Lake on OneLake is the recommended option for new models, integrates directly with OneLake security, can support tables from multiple OneLake sources, and does not use DirectQuery fallback.

options.label: Direct Lake on SQL endpoints
options.explanation: Direct Lake on SQL endpoints is coupled to a SQL analytics endpoint, is single-source for Direct Lake tables, and can use DirectQuery fallback under documented conditions.

options.label: Pure DirectQuery
options.explanation: DirectQuery queries a source at report time and does not provide the requested Direct Lake on OneLake architecture.

options.label: Import
options.explanation: Import copies data into the semantic model and requires refresh to update that copy; it is not the requested Direct Lake architecture.

questions.decisiveClue: Multiple OneLake Direct Lake sources, OneLake security, and an explicit no-fallback requirement all point to Direct Lake on OneLake.

questions.title: Choose a store for Spark and mixed file data
questions.context: Aurora’s data engineering team receives Parquet and JSON files, uses Spark notebooks for transformation, and wants curated Delta tables available in OneLake. T-SQL-only enterprise reporting is not the primary requirement.
questions.question: Which Fabric data store is the strongest fit?

options.label: Lakehouse
options.explanation: A lakehouse combines OneLake file storage and Delta tables with data-engineering and Spark workloads, matching the mixed-file and notebook requirements.

options.label: Warehouse
options.explanation: Warehouse is optimized for relational T-SQL analytics and structured warehouse workloads; it is less aligned with the stated Spark and mixed-file engineering focus.

options.label: Eventhouse
options.explanation: Eventhouse is optimized for high-volume event and time-series analytics with KQL, not general Spark-based curation of Parquet and JSON files.

options.label: Semantic model
options.explanation: A semantic model is an analytical modeling layer, not the primary storage and engineering environment requested.

questions.decisiveClue: The workload centers on Spark, files, and Delta tables in OneLake rather than T-SQL-first relational warehousing.

questions.title: Choose a store for high-volume telemetry
questions.context: Aurora receives millions of timestamped device events continuously. Analysts need fast ad hoc filtering, aggregation, and time-series analysis with KQL.
questions.question: Which Fabric store most directly fits the workload?

options.label: Eventhouse
options.explanation: Eventhouse is designed for high-volume event, telemetry, and time-series analytics using KQL.

options.label: Warehouse
options.explanation: Warehouse is designed for relational T-SQL analytics; it is not the most direct store for the stated KQL-first telemetry workload.

options.label: Lakehouse
options.explanation: Lakehouse can store large datasets, but the explicit real-time event and KQL requirements point more directly to Eventhouse.

options.label: Import semantic model
options.explanation: An Import semantic model is an analytical layer with copied data, not the event store requested for continuous telemetry.

questions.decisiveClue: The decisive clues are continuous high-volume event data and KQL-based time-series analysis.

questions.title: Understand what a OneLake shortcut points to

questions.title: Check provenance before reusing a Fabric item

questions.title: Resolve a known null-value business rule

questions.title: Add descriptive columns from a lookup table

options.explanation: Deduplication does not add customer attributes.

questions.title: Reduce transaction rows to a summary table

questions.decisiveClue: The target grain is explicitly one row per Region and Month with aggregated measures.

questions.title: Flatten a snowflaked geography hierarchy
questions.context: Aurora’s source has Store → City → Region as three normalized lookup tables. The analytics requirement is a straightforward star schema with one Store dimension used for filtering by Store, City, and Region.

options.explanation: Many-to-many relationships are not needed to represent a simple one-to-many geographic hierarchy.

options.label: Discard City and Region

questions.title: Identify the grain of a sales fact table

options.explanation: The scenario explicitly states that each product line on an order creates one fact row.

options.explanation: The same product can appear on many order lines, so Product alone does not define the grain.

options.explanation: Quantity is not a descriptive property of a date.

options.label: Nowhere in the source model; invent it only as a DAX constant

options.explanation: ProductCategory does not describe a date.

questions.title: Filter Warehouse rows before aggregation

options.label: ORDER BY
options.explanation: ORDER BY sorts the final result and does not remove source rows from the aggregation.

options.label: SELECT alone
